next_step: Finalize Dedicated pricing and sign 12-mo SOW; legal review of data residency clause
notes:
Summary: Mid-market product org building a contextual support assistant + inline summarization inside product. Started on Hosted API (quick PoC) -> promising quality but cost/latency concerns at scale. Now negotiating Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable unit economics.

History / Timeline (short):
- 2025-11-20: Intro call (AE Priya). Discussed roadmap, compliance needs.
- 2025-12-05: Hosted API trial onboarded (trial keys, sample prompts).
- 2026-01-14: 2-week Hosted API PoC results: embeddings and chat flows validated; cost model projected >$20k/mo at current traffic.
- 2026-02-08: Demo of Dedicated offering (Marco SE) — architecture, VPC option, KV cache, batching explained.
- 2026-02-18: 3-hour technical deep-dive (Fireflies ff-20260218-emberglow-demo). Validated tokenization, instruction tuning needs.
- 2026-02-25: Pricing/rates call w/ pricing team (Fireflies ff-20260225-pricing-call). Presented 3 pricing sketches and ramp options.

POC specifics / tech requirements:
- Workloads: real-time chat + async summarization + re-rank for search. Mixed short chats (avg 30 tokens) and long-context summarization (avg 2k tokens).
- Target SLOs: p95 response < 800ms for chat; p50 < 250ms for short replies; throughput target 120-200 requests/sec during peak.
- Quality: prefer open/model variants with instruction fine-tunes; some preference for variants that support structured tool/function calling.
- Data controls: VPC-only control plane, bring-your-own-KMS, audit logs per request, 13-month retention configurable.

Pricing/Packaging negotiation notes (Dedicated):
- Presented options (high level):
  * Option A — Baseline commit (Dedicated small pool) for predictable monthly cost. Baseline = 2x mid-tier GPUs equivalent; includes 20% burst capacity and 10% overage pool billed at per-hour overage rate. 12-mo term preferred.
  * Option B — 12-mo ramp schedule: months 1-3 at 50% commit (discounted), months 4-6 at 75%, month 7+ at 100%. Lower up-front commitment to reduce procurement friction.
  * Option C — Higher commit + volume credit for caching and Optimize consult (savings share). Better unit economics but requires leadership sign-off.
- Customer feedback: CTO wants predictable monthly spend; product lead pushes for ramp model to avoid upfront heavy commit. Finance wants clear overage caps.
- Key ask from Emberglow: soft cap on overage (notify at 85% utilization), ability to burst up to 2.5x baseline for 48-hour windows twice per quarter, and clear overage rate (prefer flat per-hour GPU rate vs per-token).
- Pricing sensitivity: target committed spend ~$12k-$22k/month first year, aiming toward $18k/mo steady state if performance meets SLOs.
- Negotiation tensions: Redwood pricing team proposed 15% discount for 12-mo straight commit vs ramp schedule; Emberglow requested a 25% discount + an initial 3-month credit to offset migration costs.

POC results / perf notes:
- Real-world latency on Dedicated trial (short token runs): p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 720ms (within target for chat). Long-context summarization peaks ~2.4s for 2k-token runs on single GPU; team exploring KV prefixing + quantized models to reduce time.
- Batching/Cache wins: observed ~22% token cost reduction when using prefix caching for product docs. Redwood Optimize recommendations validated in test.

Security & compliance progress:
- Asked for SOC2 Type II evidence and architecture diagram for VPC deployment. Security provided draft SOC2 binder; still need on-site audit schedule for Emberglow compliance team.
- Data residency: Emberglow requires US-only residency for customer PII; Redwood to confirm region-locking for Dedicated nodes.

Open action items / next steps:
- Pricing: Redwood to send updated SOW with 2 options (12-mo straight commit with 15% discount OR ramp schedule with 20% limited promotional credit) by 2026-03-08. (Pricing deck link in Drive).
- Legal: Emberglow legal to provide markups on SOW and master services agreement. Blocker: indemnity language and data processing addendum.
- Security: Confirm region-locking and KMS integration timeline (SEC-4390).
- Technical: Marco to provide 3rd-party e2e test harness for final perf verification (expected completion 2026-03-12).
- Sales close target: April 2026 (Forecast 2026-04).

Quotes/Direct notes from calls:
- CTO: "We like the latency numbers on Dedicated. The ask is keep spend predictable — finance won't approve big bursts without hard caps."
- Product lead: "Ramp schedule is our preference — we can start small while instrumenting traffic shaping."
- AE notes: deal likely to close if we (1) accept ramp schedule with small promo credit, (2) define clear overage cap and burst window, and (3) get legal sign-off on DPA.
